priority.override_reason: Ranks 1 through 6 are closed by current rejected direct-leaf frame, constructor, heap-value-cache, direct-eval, and RegExp evidence. The rank-7 CDJS profile found only a sub-10-percent independently removable Vm and frame construction cost, while both structural frame-reuse routes already have negative evidence. The current rank-8 profile identifies a distinct blocked shared mechanism: an otherwise scalar typed-loop-compatible numeric region is rejected because sloppy fallback locals write existing numeric global data properties. The extension is defined only by bytecode shape, binding identity, ordinary data-property state, and existing typed-loop guards; it has no workload, source-path, checksum, or iteration-count condition. This is a one-target override because it is the highest remaining viable queue item after the higher-ranked mechanisms were closed; retention still requires the strict target, control, complete external, complete broad, and exact Test262 gates below.

mechanism.summary: Extend the existing typed-loop executor to admit a scalar numeric region with StoreLocalOrGlobalSloppy fallback locals only when each fallback already resolves to the same writable ordinary numeric own-data global property, then perform each guarded global write in program order rather than batching it at loop exit.
mechanism.generality: The extension applies to every existing typed-loop-compatible scalar region whose sloppy fallback slots have stable non-shadowing binding identities and whose corresponding global own properties already exist as writable ordinary data properties. A same-name LoadGlobal is admitted only when it resolves to that exact fallback slot and is represented by the slot's scalar register, so each iteration observes its prior write; unrelated global reads remain hoisted only when they do not overlap a global write. The entry guard rejects direct eval, with-like dynamic binding paths, absent globals, accessors, proxies, non-writable properties, changed realm-cell identities, non-numeric values, unsupported observable property writes, or any unsupported bytecode. No source text, workload name, iteration count, or benchmark-specific shape is accepted; all rejected cases retain the ordinary interpreter path.
semantic_risks: a sloppy fallback must continue to resolve to its local binding when one is later introduced, and to the global property only when the original bytecode semantics select that fallback
global data-property reads and writes must preserve their existing identity checks, coercion behavior, exception timing, and program order; writes may not be deferred or coalesced across iterations

a changed Math object, accessor, proxy, descriptor, direct eval, dynamic binding, alias, or scalar-domain escape must decline admission or deopt at an exact bytecode boundary without losing completed writes
the native loop must synchronize the local fallback slot and the realm global property after every admitted write so later bytecode observes exactly the same value

profile_evidence.shared_cost: The 3,692-sample profile is dominated by Vm::run_completion, load_global, eval_binary, Value clone and drop, local-slot access, dynamic binding lookup, and generic call dispatch; Math libc work itself is small. Exact inspection shows the loop already fits the scalar typed-loop operation classes, including guarded numeric Math calls, but compilation refuses its Math global read because the same region contains StoreLocalOrGlobalSloppy writes for chained-initializer fallback globals. The current executor has no safe per-iteration fallback-global sink, so the whole region stays in generic bytecode dispatch.
